chapters.title: The Polarity Strategy: Declare War on Your Enemies
chapters.sourcePressure: People often refuse to admit real opposition because the admission feels uncivil; the cost is late, weak, confused action.
chapters.coreMove: Name the person whose gain depends on your loss, then change disclosure and access without turning tense people into enemies.
chapters.commonMisread: Treat every critic, rival, or difficult peer as an enemy and become paranoid.

chapters.title: The Guerrilla-War-of-the-Mind Strategy: Do Not Fight the Last War
chapters.sourcePressure: Previous success becomes a liability when conditions change and the mind reaches for the last war instead of the current one.
chapters.coreMove: Separate what the present situation is showing from the old victory your memory wants to replay.
chapters.commonMisread: Worship novelty or throw away useful experience just because the labels changed.

chapters.title: The Counterbalance Strategy: Do Not Lose Your Presence of Mind
chapters.sourcePressure: Anger, fear, and embarrassment narrow time horizon and make bad decisions feel clear while they are happening.
chapters.coreMove: Build a repeatable counterweight that restores width before stress chooses the next move for you.
chapters.commonMisread: Confuse presence of mind with being emotionless or with delaying every urgent decision.

chapters.title: The Death-Ground Strategy: Create a Sense of Urgency and Desperation
chapters.sourcePressure: Death ground means self-created constraint that makes retreat costly enough to sharpen focus; it is dangerous for the already overwhelmed.
chapters.coreMove: Create chosen pressure by removing respectable exits when comfort, not overload, is the real obstacle.
chapters.commonMisread: Add pressure everywhere and call burnout discipline.

chapters.title: The Command-and-Control Strategy: Avoid the Snares of Groupthink
chapters.sourcePressure: Groupthink is structural: the cost of speaking up is visible, the cost of silence is hidden, and hierarchy makes silence look safe.
chapters.coreMove: Give mission, context, and dissent channels instead of over-specifying method when the team is competent enough to adapt.
chapters.commonMisread: Replace leadership with vague autonomy or consensus with no command.

chapters.title: The Controlled-Chaos Strategy: Segment Your Forces
chapters.sourcePressure: One big structure makes one bottleneck, one bad read, or one slow committee contaminate the whole organization.
chapters.coreMove: Break a brittle monolith into capable semi-autonomous units that can fail locally and recombine around a shared purpose.
chapters.commonMisread: Assume smaller units are automatically stronger even when they lack context or competence.

chapters.title: Morale Strategies: Transform Your War into a Crusade
chapters.sourcePressure: Morale rises when labor attaches to meaning larger than tasks and when the leader visibly embodies that meaning.
chapters.coreMove: Turn sustained work into a cause by naming the opposing problem, the served purpose, and the leader behavior that proves belief.
chapters.commonMisread: Use mission language cynically as a motivation hack.

chapters.title: The Perfect-Economy Strategy: Pick Your Battles
chapters.sourcePressure: Resources are finite, and most winnable fights are still too low-value to deserve the spend.
chapters.coreMove: Spend attention, money, patience, and political capital only on fights whose win or loss changes something important.
chapters.commonMisread: Avoid conflict permanently and call it strategic economy.

chapters.title: The Counterattack Strategy: Turn the Tables
chapters.sourcePressure: The opponent who attacks first commits force, exposes intent, and often leans too far forward; timing decides whether the return lands.
chapters.coreMove: Absorb an opening attack long enough to see what it reveals, then answer through the exposed gap before balance returns.
chapters.commonMisread: Retaliate instantly or wait passively forever.

chapters.title: Deterrence Strategies: Create a Threatening Presence
chapters.sourcePressure: Deterrence works before the exchange begins by shaping the other side's calculation, but it collapses if the threat is bluff.
chapters.coreMove: Make the real cost of attacking visible enough that a rational opponent chooses not to start.
chapters.commonMisread: Perform toughness without actual capacity.

chapters.title: The Nonengagement Strategy: Trade Space for Time
chapters.sourcePressure: When the opponent is stronger, standing on their chosen ground wastes force; withdrawal buys time only if there is strategic depth.
chapters.coreMove: Yield ground you can afford to lose so time, endurance, and overextension begin working against the stronger side.
chapters.commonMisread: Retreat from a position that has no survivable ground to trade.

chapters.title: Grand Strategy: Lose Battles but Win the War
chapters.sourcePressure: Without grand strategy, local victories feel good but do not add up; with it, some losses are useful because they buy the larger design.
chapters.coreMove: Judge every short-term win or loss by whether it serves the long-horizon campaign you have explicitly named.
chapters.commonMisread: Make a rigid life plan and defend it after reality changes.

chapters.title: The Intelligence Strategy: Know Your Enemy
chapters.sourcePressure: Failed attacks often strike an imagined opponent because surface stories hide true incentives and vulnerabilities.
chapters.coreMove: Act against the opponent that actually exists by mapping motives, resources, allies, fears, and internal tensions before the move.
chapters.commonMisread: Research forever as a socially acceptable way to avoid acting.

chapters.title: The Blitzkrieg Strategy: Overwhelm Resistance with Speed and Suddenness
chapters.sourcePressure: Speed is a weapon when operational tempo outpaces resistance, but only when paired with judgment.
chapters.coreMove: Tighten observation, orientation, decision, and action until the other side keeps answering positions you have already left.
chapters.commonMisread: Move fast in the wrong direction and treat motion as strategy.

chapters.title: Forcing Strategies: Control the Dynamic
chapters.sourcePressure: Initiative means controlling the dynamic before the engagement appears to start; agenda and sequence are strategic tools.
chapters.coreMove: Set the time, place, sequence, pace, and frame so the other side is answering your chosen terms.
chapters.commonMisread: Act aggressively just to feel in charge.

chapters.title: The Center-of-Gravity Strategy: Hit Them Where It Hurts
chapters.sourcePressure: The center of gravity is rarely the visible strength; misidentifying it wastes force and exposes the attacker.
chapters.coreMove: Find the load-bearing point whose weakening makes the opponent's whole position harder to sustain, then ignore louder secondary targets.
chapters.commonMisread: Hit the most obvious or emotionally satisfying target.

chapters.title: The Divide-and-Conquer Strategy: Defeat Them in Detail
chapters.sourcePressure: A united opponent is stronger than its parts; a divided one is weaker, but a clumsy wedge can create solidarity.
chapters.coreMove: Loosen a coalition by finding a real existing disagreement and dealing with the fragments after unity weakens.
chapters.commonMisread: Invent division or attack noisily enough to unify the other side.

chapters.title: The Turning Strategy: Expose and Attack Your Opponent's Soft Flank
chapters.sourcePressure: Every defense has a strong front and a softer flank; reconnaissance and patience beat charging the obvious target.
chapters.coreMove: Refuse the strong front and find the dimension where the opponent is structurally least prepared to adapt.
chapters.commonMisread: Keep searching for a clever flank when none exists and lose initiative.

chapters.title: The Annihilation Strategy: Envelop the Enemy
chapters.sourcePressure: Envelopment denies retreat, support, and recomposition, but it is high-cost and catastrophic if attempted without decisive advantage.
chapters.coreMove: Close every meaningful escape path only when you already have the resources and reason to complete the encirclement.
chapters.commonMisread: Use total pressure as a routine tactic or moral thrill.

chapters.title: The Ripening-for-the-Sickle Strategy: Maneuver Them into Weakness
chapters.sourcePressure: The decisive move is often delayed; the setup does the work by making each later option worse.
chapters.coreMove: Narrow the opponent's future options through deliberate small moves until the final weak position is partly self-made.
chapters.commonMisread: Wait passively and call it maneuver.

chapters.title: The Diplomatic-War Strategy: Negotiate While Advancing
chapters.sourcePressure: Diplomacy and pressure work together when the channel is sincere and the pressure makes the off-ramp attractive.
chapters.coreMove: Press materially while keeping a real face-saving off-ramp open, so settlement feels like relief rather than surrender.
chapters.commonMisread: Use negotiation as decoration while demanding humiliation.

chapters.title: The Exit Strategy: Know How to End Things
chapters.sourcePressure: Exit is hardest when prior investment, public commitment, and ego argue for staying beyond the best available terms.
chapters.coreMove: Precommit exit conditions before identity and sunk cost make staying feel noble after the campaign has turned bad.
chapters.commonMisread: Quit whenever persistence feels uncomfortable.

chapters.title: Misperception Strategies: Weave a Seamless Blend of Fact and Fiction
chapters.sourcePressure: Misperception strategy sits on the ethical edge between legitimate framing and propaganda; the teaching must make that line explicit.
chapters.coreMove: Shape perception by sequencing true facts clearly, while refusing any frame that depends on false belief or hidden distortion.
chapters.commonMisread: Lie smoothly and call it strategic framing.

chapters.title: The Ordinary-Extraordinary Strategy: Take the Line of Least Expectation
chapters.sourcePressure: Opponents act against their forecast of your pattern; the right break may be ordinary or extraordinary depending on what they expect.
chapters.coreMove: Deny opponents a usable forecast by varying outward texture while keeping the objective stable.
chapters.commonMisread: Thrash randomly until nobody, including your side, knows the plan.

chapters.title: The Righteous Strategy: Occupy the Moral High Ground
chapters.sourcePressure: In watched conflicts, the side read as just gains structural advantage, but one hypocrisy can collapse the posture instantly.
chapters.coreMove: Occupy moral high ground by aligning conduct and language before observers begin assigning aggressor and victim roles.
chapters.commonMisread: Treat morality as optics while behavior contradicts the claim.

chapters.title: The Strategy of the Void: Deny Them Targets
chapters.sourcePressure: A weaker operator survives by removing the fixed center, public face, or central node the stronger opponent wants to strike.
chapters.coreMove: Deny efficient attack by distributing the target while preserving enough coherence to keep acting.
chapters.commonMisread: Become so diffuse that nobody can decide or execute.

chapters.title: The Alliance Strategy: Seem to Work for the Interests of Others While Furthering Your Own
chapters.sourcePressure: Alliance works through real aligned interests, not flattery or dependence; fake overlap collapses under scrutiny.
chapters.coreMove: Borrow force from stronger actors by finding genuine overlap where your progress helps them win something they already want.
chapters.commonMisread: Mistake borrowed leverage for loyalty.

chapters.title: The One-Upmanship Strategy: Give Your Rivals Enough Rope to Hang Themselves
chapters.sourcePressure: One-upmanship is disciplined noninterference with rivals already damaged by ego, faction, or overreach.
chapters.coreMove: Let a self-defeating rival keep carrying the burden when your attack would rescue them by creating unity or sympathy.
chapters.commonMisread: Do nothing in every contest and call it restraint.

chapters.title: The Fait Accompli Strategy: Take Small Bites
chapters.sourcePressure: Opponents often judge each step in isolation and notice the aggregate too late; the ethical line is threshold management versus concealed coercion.
chapters.coreMove: Sequence small legitimate moves below reaction threshold while watching the cumulative effect as one strategic whole.
chapters.commonMisread: Hide a major harmful change through salami tactics.

chapters.title: Communication Strategies: Penetrate Their Minds
chapters.sourcePressure: Communication can persuade respectfully or manipulate by bypassing reflection; the distinction must stay explicit.
chapters.coreMove: Enter the audience's frame so communication answers their real decision instead of displaying your own intelligence.
chapters.commonMisread: Polish language until it sounds clever to the speaker but misses the receiver's filters.

chapters.title: The Inner-Front Strategy: Destroy from Within
chapters.sourcePressure: Some opponents cohere against external pressure and weaken only when their own tensions become unmanageable.
chapters.coreMove: Pressure real internal contradictions without manufacturing mistrust or healing the target through clumsy frontal attack.
chapters.commonMisread: Plant lies or fracture ordinary groups for advantage.

chapters.title: The Passive-Aggression Strategy: Dominate While Seeming to Submit
chapters.sourcePressure: A weaker operator can be crushed by open resistance too early; hidden construction can be prudent or corrosive depending on whether open disagreement was available.
chapters.coreMove: Under real asymmetry, comply outwardly while quietly building options until direct challenge becomes survivable.
chapters.commonMisread: Use indirect undermining where honest dissent or exit was possible.

chapters.title: The Chain-Reaction Strategy: Sow Uncertainty and Panic Through Acts of Terror
chapters.sourcePressure: A small unexpected move can produce disproportionate psychological effect, but the legitimate version breaks assumptions rather than inducing terror.
chapters.coreMove: Use bounded surprise to force recalibration without relying on fear, panic, humiliation, or threat theater.
chapters.commonMisread: Intimidate people and call the panic strategic.
